name: Radiohead
hook: A guitar band whose singer stopped listening to guitar music, played Warp records instead, and turned the band into something closer to Aphex Twin and Can for 'Kid A'.

blurb.age13: Radiohead formed at school in Abingdon, near Oxford, in 1985. Their first hit, 'Creep' (1992), was a loud guitar song, and they got tired of it. 'OK Computer' (1997) was much stranger, and the singer Thom Yorke said Miles Davis's 'Bitches Brew' had influenced it. By the late 1990s Yorke was listening almost only to electronic music from the Warp label, like Aphex Twin and Autechre, because it had structure and no singing in it. On 'Kid A' (2000) the band used drum machines, synthesizers and computers as much as guitars. They also named the German band Can, jazz, and Björk as influences. In 2007 they let fans pay whatever they wanted for 'In Rainbows', even nothing.
blurb.adult: Formed in Abingdon in 1985 as On a Friday by Thom Yorke, Jonny and Colin Greenwood, Ed O'Brien and Philip Selway, and signed to EMI in December 1991. 'Creep' (1992) was a worldwide hit the band came to resent. Yorke has cited 'Bitches Brew' as an influence on 'OK Computer' (1997). For 'Kid A' (2 October 2000), produced with Nigel Godrich, Yorke had turned away from rock and melody and was listening almost exclusively to Warp artists such as Aphex Twin and Autechre; the band also drew on Can, Charles Mingus, Alice Coltrane, Miles Davis, Talking Heads' 'Remain in Light' and Björk's 'Homogenic', and used modular synthesizers, the ondes Martenot, and editing in Pro Tools and Cubase. 'In Rainbows' (2007) was self-released online at a price the buyer chose, the first time a major act had done so.
